title: Metrics, dimensions and definitions shared between teams

videos.script: Three people quote last quarter's revenue in the same meeting. Marketing says three hundred and twenty-nine thousand reais. Finance says two hundred and ninety-four thousand. {{three}} Nobody made a mistake. They used the same word for three different definitions. {{word}} This lesson takes a metric apart. A column, a way of adding it up, a filter, a date in a time zone, and a person who owns it. {{parts}} Then the things you slice by, which turn out to need definitions too. One column called channel means two different things in two tables. {{channel}} Then the traps inside the arithmetic. An average that can be taken two ways. A day that begins at a different moment depending on the clock. {{clock}} And finally, what to do when two numbers disagree. You build a bridge, one step per difference, and check that it closes. {{bridge}} By the end, revenue at Lantern means one thing, written down where every tool and every person reads it. {{end}}
